extracted.intended_audience: people inspecting or studying manufactories (industrial observers, inspectors, engineers, students of political economy)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical method for visiting, recording, and reporting on manufactories: what to ask, what to record for each process, and how to verify numerical and qualitative information gathered during factory observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt recording of information
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to commit to writing all information as soon as possible after it is received, especially when numbers are concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing while visiting may interrupt the examination of machinery; when immediate writing is impossible, record as soon as you can. Emphasizes timeliness to preserve accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare questions and skeleton forms beforehand
rubrics_metrics.description: Have prepared beforehand the questions to be asked, and leave blanks for the answers, which may be quickly inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a list tailored to each manufacture, better drawn up after a first visit. Save time by printing and binding skeleton forms into a pocket-book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use printed pocket-book of skeleton forms
rubrics_metrics.description: To save time, have printed and bound in a pocket-book a hundred copies of the skeleton forms for processes, with about twenty of the general inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized forms speed data collection and ensure comparable information across visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief sketch of history
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines should contain a brief sketch of its history, particularly the date of its invention and its introduction into England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include historical context as part of the description of any mechanical art or manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous states and sourcing of material
rubrics_metrics.description: Short reference to the previous states through which the material employed has passed; the places whence it is procured; the price of a given quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document supply chain, raw-material treatment, and procurement costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential description of processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The various processes must be described successively according to the plan given in §129.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a step-by-step account of each process, with sufficient detail to reproduce or evaluate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of production of different kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Are various kinds of the same article made in one establishment, or at different ones, and are there differences in the processes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether product variants are produced in-house or outsourced and note process differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects to which goods are liable
rubrics_metrics.description: To what defects are the goods liable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List common failure modes, durability issues, and quality weaknesses observed or reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutes and adulterations used
rubrics_metrics.description: What substitutes or adulterations are used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any fraudulent or cost-cutting materials and practices that affect quality or honesty of product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste allowed by the master
rubrics_metrics.description: What waste is allowed by the master?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record tolerances for rejects, scrap rates, and policies for damaged items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of goodness (quality tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: What tests are there of the goodness of the manufactured article?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document objective and subjective tests, measurement methods, and acceptance criteria used by the manufactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight and material yield comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The weight of a given quantity, and a comparison with that of the raw material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record finished-product weight per unit area/length/number and compare with raw input to estimate losses and yield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholesale price at manufactory
rubrics_metrics.description: The wholesale price at the manufactory ( £. s. d. per ... ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record factory gate pricing for the product in standard units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usual retail price
rubrics_metrics.description: The usual retail price ( £. s. d. per ... ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record market/retail prices to compare margins and distribution effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and repair of tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Who provide tools? Master, or men? Who repair tools? Master, or men?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document responsibility for capital vs. labor-supplied tools and maintenance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense of machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the expense of the machinery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record purchase cost, installation expenses, and capital outlay for key machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual wear and tear and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the annual wear and tear, and what its duration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate depreciation, maintenance intervals, and expected service life of machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular trade for making machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any particular trade for making it? Where?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specialized trades or regions that manufacture or service the machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is machinery made and repaired on site
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it made and repaired at the manufactory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note in-house manufacturing/repair capabilities vs external suppliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes, workforce numbers, and output
rubrics_metrics.description: In any manufactory visited, state the number ( ) of processes, and of the persons employed in each process, and the quantity of manufactured produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide process-by-process headcounts and production volumes for throughput analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual national production quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: What quantity is made annually in Great Britain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, contextualize the local manufactory output within national production figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital investment scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the capital invested in manufactories large or small?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess capital intensity and scale of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal manufacturing locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention the principal seats of this manufacture in England; and if it flourishes much abroad, the places where it is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map geographic centers of the industry domestically and internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes, bounties, and trade flows
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty, excise, or bounty, if any, should be stated, and any alterations in past years; and also the amount exported or imported for a series of years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record fiscal regime and trade statistics affecting the industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imports comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same article, but of superior, equal, or inferior make, is imported?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess competition from imports by quality tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channel (export or middleman)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manufacturer export, or sell, to a middleman, who supplies the merchant?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the distribution chain and whether the producer deals directly with buyers or via intermediaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export destinations and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: To what countries is it chiefly sent — and in what goods are the returns made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document principal export markets and barter/trade return composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-specific: place/name/date
rubrics_metrics.description: Process ( ) Manufacture ( ) Place ( ) Name ( ) date 183_.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-matter for each process skeleton to uniquely identify the operation and record the visit date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process mode and tool sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: The mode of executing it, with sketches of the tools or machine if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough procedural detail and diagrammatic sketches to convey how the operation is performed and what equipment is employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of attendants per machine
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of persons necessary to attend the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record staffing per machine for labor-efficiency calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative composition by gender/age
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the operatives men, ( ) women, ( ) or children? If mixed, what are the proportions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document workforce demographics and proportions for social and capacity analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages/pay per operative class
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the pay of each? ( s. d.) ( s. d.) ( s. d.) per ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record pay rates per class/category and unit (per day, per piece).

rubrics_metrics.name: Working hours per day
rubrics_metrics.description: What number ( ) of hours do they work per day?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record normal working day length and any variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Night-and-day continuous operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it usual, or necessary, to work night and day without stopping?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether continuous operation (24/7 shifts) is practiced and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piecework vs day-work
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the labour performed by piece or by day-work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document compensation system, as it affects productivity and incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill requirement and apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: What degree of skill is required, and how many years ( ) apprenticeship?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess training needs and barriers to entry for the occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation repetition rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of times ( ) the operation is repeated per day or per hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record cycle rates or throughput per time unit for capacity analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure rate metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of failures ( ) in a thousand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record defect/failure incidence per thousand to quantify quality control performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for damaged articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the workman or the master loses by the broken or damaged articles? What is done with them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document accountability for scrap and repair/disposal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of repeated operations on measure and loss
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same process is repeated several times, state the diminution or increase of measure, and the loss, if any, at each repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track cumulative dimensional changes and material losses across repeated processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use printed multiple-choice answers for speed
rubrics_metrics.description: In using this skeleton, the answers to the questions are in some cases printed, as 'Who repair the tools? Masters, Men', so that the proper answer may be underlined with a pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design forms with common options pre-printed to speed completion and reduce transcription errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid observer effect when measuring speed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the observer stands with his watch in his hand before a person, the workman will almost certainly increase his speed, and the estimate will be too large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer asking what is considered a fair day's work or use unobtrusive measurements (e.g., count loom strokes by sound from outside) rather than overt timed observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer reported fair-day metrics or covert observation
rubrics_metrics.description: A much better average will result from inquiring what quantity is considered a fair day's work. When this cannot be ascertained, covert observation methods may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indirect measures (machine noise, unattended counts) to estimate typical rates without altering worker behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify answers by cross-calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers which are given directly may also be deduced by a short calculation from others that are given or known; advantage should be taken of these verifications to confirm accuracy or correct anomalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform quick consistency checks among responses (e.g., production rate vs output) and reconcile discordant data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include control questions to gauge respondent's judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable to have an estimate of the soundness of a person's judgment; the questions can be so shaped that some of them may indirectly depend on others, and one or two may be inserted whose answers can be obtained by other methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-questions and verifiable items to assess reliability of informants and calibrate your own judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice pre-measure estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: The habit of forming an estimate of the magnitude or frequency of any object immediately previous to our applying to it measure or number, tends materially to fix our attention and to improve our judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make and note an a priori estimate before measuring; compare afterward to improve assessment skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe repeatedly and at different times (Coulomb's caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coulomb cautions observers against being deceived by single short observations: observe the workmen at different times in the day, without their knowledge, and measure results after several days of continuous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on brief (e.g., 11-minute) observations; collect repeated samples over time to avoid bias and obtain representative averages.
